newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks to let broker's clients use ATM.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks to let broker's clients use ATM.

text.p: Japan's top 10 commercial banks have agreed to allow clients of securities houses to withdraw money and check their balances through the banks' nationwide automatic teller machine (ATM) networks, banking industry sources said on Friday.
The Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA), which has been asking for access to the ATM networks since last November, has been told of the decision, the sources said.

They said that the securities houses would probably be able to use the ATM networks of the 10 big commercial banks some time in the next financial year starting next April after the details of the usage are settled, such as the commissions brokers and their clients must pay the banks.

As part of Japan's "Big Bang" financial deregulations, securities houses are to be allowed to start offering multi-service accounts in the 1997/98 business year to enable customers to transfer profits automatically from stock sales into money management funds.
The securities industry has been keen to make use of the ATM network of not only the top commercial banks but also regional banks to start multi-service accounts.
